summary: Klamath County lookout on Shake Butte near Bly: built 1931, rebuilt as a steel tower in the early 1950s, used for emergencies in the 1970s and now gone; no source describes the site today.

facts.design: Steel tower about 30 to 31 feet tall with a 10 by 10 foot cab (1950 per the register; 1954 per firelookout.com and the Rex page)
facts.status_note: Used for emergencies in the 1970s; the register and firelookout.com say it is now gone. No source gives the year it came down.

staffing.status: Lookouts stationed in 1940, 1943 and 1948, and a 1967 fire was spotted from the tower; no end-of-staffing date in these sources

events.note: Road, telephone line and small lookout tower built, per the KFPA 1931 annual report; firelookout.com says a cab on a rock outcrop and a cabin
Register says a cabin was built here in 1933
Lookout staffed for 180 days; reporting station Bly Station
Mrs. Rosella Cline Thompson stationed at the butte; her husband was to be the warden
Lookouts saw a balloon come down in their area in the summer of 1945; it was never found (Herald and News, August 1945)
Relief lookout covered the station over the Fourth of July holiday
Register: cabin replaced in 1950 with a 30-foot steel tower with 10x10 cab
firelookout.com and the Rex page date the 30/31-foot steel tower with 10x10 cab to 1954; the Rex page says it was 90 percent complete that year
New steel steps on the tower finished and put into use
Lightning-caused ground fire in a snag, spotted by the Shake Butte lookout; a crew put it out
Date registered June 10, 2011 per the Former Fire Lookout Sites Register

resolved_conflicts.explanation: firelookout.com gives 1931 for a cab on a rock outcrop and cabin. The Rex page quotes the 1931 KFPA annual report on a road, telephone line and small tower. The register says a cabin built in 1933. The story reports 1931 and the register's 1933 cabin.

The register dates the 30-foot steel tower with 10x10 cab to 1950. firelookout.com and the Rex page date it to 1954, with the Rex page saying it was 90 percent complete that year. The story reports both dates.
The register and firelookout.com give 30 feet for the steel tower; the Rex page gives 31 feet. The brief's 9.4 m is close to 31 feet.
firelookout.com says 17 miles NNE of Bly; the survey station description quoted on the Rex page says about 18 miles airline north of Bly.

notes_for_editor: No source describes what remains on the summit today or whether it is open to visitors, so access is omitted. The removal year is not given: the register and firelookout.com say only that it is now gone, and the Rex page has an undated Removed entry. The brief's height 9.4 m is kept because it is close to the 31 feet on the Rex page; the register and firelookout.com say 30 feet. FFLOS shows 1951 and 1964 photos (Ron Kemnow collection) and firelookout.com credits Howard Verschoor, but no image URLs were captured, so no photos are listed. The 1945 balloon item is a local sighting report and is kept short.
